fluff.overview: The Buffalo is a 100-ton large-class civilian hovertruck developed during the Star League era for the Terran Hegemony Supply and Support Services. Its designation (BFFL, standing for Behind Friendly-lines, Fixed Logistics) reflects the vehicle's intended purpose as a rear-echelon cargo hauler. The design's origins trace to the entrepreneurial vision of Jarod Westphal, a veteran of the Hegemony Armed Forces Logistics Command who recognized the commercial potential of surplus military transports at the end of his service. Westphal restored ten older BFFLs, founded Westphal Cargo Carriers Company, and secured a contract with the New Earth Trading Company, which eventually purchased his firm outright. NETC then used its licensing network to spread the design across the Inner Sphere through its CargoCrawlers division. The Buffalo's combination of hover mobility, high cargo capacity, and straightforward maintenance made it one of the most enduring logistics vehicles of its era.
fluff.capabilities: The Buffalo is powered by a fuel-cell electric engine, providing a cruise speed of 27 kilometers per hour and a flank speed of 43 kilometers per hour. Its large-class hover propulsion system allows it to cross both improved roads and open terrain, an advantage for supply operations in varied environments. The vehicle's primary value lies in its cargo capacity: four universal container hardpoints accommodate 40 tons of supplies, and a crew of three operates from a basic cab configuration. Armor protection is deliberately light (less than a ton of BAR 2-rated material) as the design was intended for rear-echelon operations rather than combat exposure. The fuel-cell power plant generates no waste heat, eliminating thermal management concerns entirely. No weapons are mounted in the standard configuration, and the Buffalo depends on escort forces or favorable positioning to avoid hostile contact. The transmission system is the vehicle's most mechanically demanding component, though improvements in available materials in later production runs simplified maintenance considerably.
fluff.deployment: The Buffalo serves as a general-purpose cargo hauler wherever rear-echelon logistics support is required. Military formations use it to shuttle ammunition, spare parts, rations, and replacement equipment between depots and forward staging areas. Commercial operators have employed the design on dozens of worlds for industrial freight, agricultural distribution, and surface transport, capitalizing on its hover capability to reach locations inaccessible to wheeled vehicles. Because the Buffalo carries no defensive systems, operators in contested territory depend on escort detachments or operate only in secured zones. The design's broad licensing history means vehicles of varying age and mechanical condition can be found across the Inner Sphere's diverse supply networks.
fluff.history:
The Buffalo entered service with the Terran Hegemony Supply and Support Services during the Star League era, gaining a reputation as a practical and undemanding logistics platform. On New Earth, Jarod Westphal's commercial venture brought the aging design back into organized production, and the New Earth Trading Company's acquisition of his firm secured a stable manufacturing base. NETC extended licensing across the Inner Sphere through its CargoCrawlers division, establishing New Earth as the primary production point while supporting manufacturing at multiple sites.

The collapse of the Star League had minimal impact on the Buffalo's commercial standing. Unlike combat vehicles whose manufacturers often suspended production during the Succession Wars, demand for cargo transport persisted regardless of political alignment. New Earth passed through the hands of the Lyran Commonwealth, the Federated Commonwealth during the 3040s merger, and back to Lyran control through the Civil War. The design's one significant evolution came through metallurgical advances recovered from the Helm Memory Core, which permitted the use of lighter transmission materials as that knowledge spread through the Inner Sphere.

The Buffalo's ubiquity and open cargo bay made it a recurring choice for improvised weaponization. During Anton Marik's rebellion against his brother Janos, loyalist forces on New Delos loaded surplus Buffalos with explosives and remote-control systems and deployed them against Wolf's Dragoons' Delta Regiment. The detonations were powerful enough to convince elements of Summer's Company they were under tactical nuclear attack, inflicting heavy casualties before the nature of the threat was identified. Word of Blake forces revisited the concept during the Jihad, deploying converted Buffalo drones extensively in urban combat zones, with documented examples including military-grade armor and, in some reports, actual nuclear payloads. Word of Blake forces seized New Earth during the Jihad, and production records from that occupation remain uncertain. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere administered New Earth's facilities, though the Buffalo's production status grew unclear as the Dark Age progressed.
